flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about yourself and why early childhood education matters to you.
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q1 Attempt 1]
Well, I've been dealing, you know, with kids for basically my whole life. You know, I was a teenager. I babysat. And then I became a teacher. You know, I got older. And I had a home daycare out of my house, you know, for a couple years. And what else? You know, just been around kids my whole life, basically. I work with kids on Wednesdays night now and Sunday, sometimes Sunday mornings. So I'm always around kids. So that's why I want, you know, to go back to, you know, child development stuff, you know, to be a teacher or an aide or just, you know, help out in the office, whatever's needed.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child was having a really hard moment emotionally. What did you notice about what they were feeling, and how did you respond?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q3 Attempt 1]
I just went up there and asked the child, you know, what's going on, if they can talk. You know, some kids can't talk. So you just, if they don't talk, you just look and see, okay, what could happen? Or look at their body. Maybe they fell, you know, just comfort them, you know, give them hugs, tell them it's okay. And just find out what went wrong, basically. And you just deal with it that way. And then you go on with that, you know, just take steps.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you felt overwhelmed at work with children present. What did you do to manage yourself?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q4 Attempt 1]
You just, you know, take a deep breath, you know, count, you know, to like five or seven, you know, and just say, OK, you know, you have to keep going and you just go. You know, you can't. That's part of working with kids is a lot of, you know, sometimes stressful. So you just have to deal with it and just take a deep breath and go on.

well you explained to the child you know we need to get this done you know you want do you want to go outside do you want to go play with your toys you know you need to get this done before we can do that and you just you know talk to him you know talk to the child through it and um and you know hopefully they will respond to that if not you just keep you know talking to the child finding out why they don't want to get their diaper changed or put their jacket on or you know so you just find out what's going on and talk to them you know they talked about communication that why you know why are they feeling that

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you had to work closely with another adult in a challenging situation. How did you navigate it?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q8 Attempt 1]
Um, it, it happens a lot, you know, when you're working with other people and you just, like I say, you know, communication, just, you know, talk, talk to them and say, Hey, you know, why are we, you know, what's going on and, you know, how can we fix it? And why do you think that way? And why do I think that way? And just, just go with it, you know, and just see how you can work it out as a team, you know, you know, when you work at school or, you know, you're working as a team and everybody has to, you know, communicate and find a way of working.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Can you share something you’ve learned about children or yourself over time that changed how you approach your work?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q9 Attempt 1]
Have a lot of patience, you know, um, yeah, patience is the key. Um, you know, with working with kids and working with coworkers, you just have to be patient with each other and, you know, it just, and just take time and, you know, and take breaks when you need it, ask for help if you need it or pitch in when somebody needs to help, you know, when you see it, you know, a coworker struggling or maybe need a break or something, you just say, Hey, do you need just have like a five second break or a five minute break and you just pitch in when needed.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child’s behavior was challenging for you. How did you approach it?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q10 Attempt 1]
What was the question? Just talk to them. You know, just ask them, you know, what's going on. Or if they don't talk, you know, you see, okay, what's the situation? What happened? Did a child, you know, throw a toy at them or, you know, or did they just having a bad day and they just need somebody to talk to? A lot of times kids have bad days and they just need somebody to talk to and give hugs and pet them and then they'd be fine, you know. And you just have to, you know, get to know the child, you know. And, yeah, so just to get to know the child and talk to them and find out what's going on.
